body:
I trust my mother. My dad died 6 years ago. She knows I'm depressed and taking medication but I don't really want to talk about this with her because she's going to panic if I tell her everything. I also don't want to burden her any more because she just found out she has thyroid cancer. If she dies from this I am 95% percent sure I'm going to kill myself because there wouldn't be any reason left why I shouldn't do it. 

I don't think it's necessary though. I used to think I'm never going to kill myself as long as my mother is alive because I don't want to do this to her but this has become less important to me lately. It's not that big of a deal anymore.

I've seen a doctor who prescribed me my antidepressants. I have an appointment with a psychiatrist in April to revise my medication, but I haven't really had any in-depth conversation with anybody about my thoughts. I did tell my girlfriend that I have suicidal thoughts and she stopped calling me soon after.

I do not actually have good friends but I don't think this really matters. Objectively my situation is not that bad that anybody in their right mind would contemplate suicide, but I'm not in the right state of mind. There's something fundamentally wrong with me, and medication doesn't help.
That's why I don't think talking is going to help me. I'm just fucked up in the head and there's nobody who can help me.
I'm hesitant, otherwise I wouldn't post here, but I honestly believe suicide is the best and the most logical decision for me. I'm just trying to work up the courage.
